The system should respond quickly enough during incidents when staff may be making multiple changes or checking server status quickly.
Loading screens should feel immediate.
The system shall present validation messages that are specific, plain, and tied directly to the field or setting that caused the problem.
The system shall support multiple administrators working at the same time without users overwriting each other’s changes.
The system shall provide locking or conflict detection for critical records.
Warnings shall clearly indicate whether a problem is a simple data issue or a conflict with another user's change.
Critical incident-related warnings shall be visually distinct from routine validation errors.
The system shall keep core screens and incident monitoring responsive when several users are in the system at once.
Routine issues shall be handled in a standard way.
The migration must carry over the current configuration without breaking branch operations.
The centralized administration module must account for local settings and permissions that may not map cleanly into a single centralized module.
The migration must carefully review user accounts.
The migration should preserve audit history where possible.
The migration should be phased and well-tested.
The migration should validate each piece before switching over.
The system shall clean up duplicate or inconsistent user and group records during data migration.
The system shall normalize branch names during data migration.
The system shall normalize role names during data migration.
The system shall normalize configuration values during data migration so they follow one standard format.
The system shall flag older entries that do not meet the new validation rules for manual review instead of forcing invalid data through.
The system shall include a reconciliation step to verify that converted data matches what the old system actually had.
The reconciliation step shall especially cover privileges and audit-related data.
Some branches may have custom settings or exceptions that are not obvious until migration time.
Custom settings or exceptions could be lost during migration if they are not handled carefully.
Custom settings or exceptions could be applied too broadly during migration if they are not handled carefully.
The migration process shall include special handling for permissions.
The migration process shall include special handling for service schedules.
The migration process shall include special handling for interface settings.
The migration process shall include special handling for branch-specific workflows built up over time.
The cutover should be timed so that daily service is not interrupted.
High-risk items should be migrated and verified in stages.
The migration process shall start with a full inventory of the existing system.
The migration process shall include a mapping exercise to determine how each item fits the new module.
The system shall support a test migration in a nonproduction environment.
The test migration shall validate users and permissions first, then configurations, then audit data.
The migration process shall proceed only after each part matches expectations.
Before cutover, the migration shall require sign-off from the admins who actually use the functions being migrated.
Each migration stage shall have a clear pass/fail check.
The system shall allow sufficient time to compare migrated data and behavior against the old system before advancing to the next stage.
The migration process shall roll back if permissions do not match closely enough.
The migration process shall roll back if configurations do not match closely enough.
The migration process shall roll back if audit records do not match closely enough.
The migration process shall roll back if there is any sign that branch workflows would be disrupted.
Issues found during migration shall be logged.
Issues found during migration shall be assigned.
Issues found during migration shall be retested in a controlled way before the next phase proceeds.
A few branch managers or lead staff should be involved in validating migrated data and configurations.
Branch managers or lead staff should validate configurations because they are often the first to notice when a configuration does not match real-world workflow.
If security, networking, or database staff are impacted by the change, they should review their parts of the change.
Security, networking, or database staff should review anything related to access, interfaces, or backups when they are impacted by the change.
Operational staff who understand daily branch impact should have a chance to confirm that changes affecting public service indirectly look right.
